description: hasHl derivation is a substring regex over a free-text positions summary: prompt.mjs:192 `/\bhl\b|hyperliquid|perp|long|short/i.test(ctx.positionsSummary || '')`. The actual positionsSummary produced in production (index.mjs:210-211) is a YIELD summary string like '~$12 in yield-beefy (last tx 0xabcd...)'. It contains NO 'hl/hyperliquid/perp/long/short' token, so hasHl is FALSE even when the agent's portfolio is yield. That is correct for yield, but the derivation is fragile in both directions: (1) FALSE-NEGATIVE — the production summarizer (index.mjs:208) only ever looks for ledger lines whose source startsWith('yield'); it NEVER summarizes an actual open HL position. So in the real path positionsSummary can never contain an HL token, meaning the 'WITH an HL position -> close' branch is effectively dead code in production and the agent holding a real perp will be told to 'withdraw idle yield' (wrong steer). (2) FALSE-POSITIVE — `/long|short/i` matches inside unrelated words ('longshot', 'long-term goal', 'shortfall', 'belong'); a genesisPrompt or yield label containing such a word would flip hasHl true and mis-steer toward 'close an HL position' that does not exist. \bhl\b also matches a bare 'HL' anywhere. No test exercises either false case (the tests only feed the clean strings 'HL ETH long 2x' and '').
